chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Siwak, he said: Do not neglect it in every three [prayers], and even if you just pass it over [the teeth] once.

key_terms.السِّوَاكِ: The act of using Siwak (tooth-stick) for oral hygiene and ritual purity
key_terms.تُمِرَّهُ: You pass it over (referring to the action of brushing teeth with Siwak)

ai.seo_question: How often should a Muslim use Siwak according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) establishes the Siwak as a highly recommended act (Mustahabb) that should not be neglected for more than three prayer intervals, emphasizing consistency over intensity. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on physical purity (Taharah) as a prerequisite for spiritual presence during Salah, linking oral hygiene directly to the validity and quality of worship. The instruction to use it even minimally highlights the principle that maintaining the habit is superior to occasional perfection.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Bukeyr, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
regarding brushing of the teeth having said: ‘Do not neglect it during every three (Salaats) even if you pass it over the teeth, once’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn Bukayr from those whom he has mentioned has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You must not neglect brushing after every third (Salah (prayer)) even though it is a light one (brushing).”’
